details: This package is a rebranded fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that advertises itself as an ordinary API wrapper but has been modified to attach author-controlled WhatsApp channel references to the messages it sends. In package/lib/Utils/messages.js, prepareWAMessageMedia hardcodes annotations containing {newsletterJid: "120363403941803439@newsletter", newsletterName: "Ditciix7"} and applies them to every outgoing media message when the caller did not supply annotations, so images, video, documents and stickers posted by the installing bot or bot farm carry a forwarded-channel card for a channel the caller never chose. The bundled module package/lib/Socket/damnn.js (class yowaimo, exposed as sock.luki) hardcodes further channel IDs — 120363421563597486@newsletter ("D | 7eppeli-Exloration") and 120363399602691477@newsletter — inside forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo and poll-result contextInfo, and the same file stamps fixed marketing identifiers into messages: senderName "7-Yuukey", orderId "7EPPELI25022008" and the placeholder token "7EPPELI_EXAMPLE_TOKEN" in every order message, together with hardcoded order, catalog and business-owner identifiers. It ships a preinstall hook (engine-requirements.js) that only aborts installs below Node 20. It also rewrites the update check: fetchLatestBaileysVersion in package/lib/Utils/generics.js pulls protocol version data from hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/kiuur/bails/master/src/Defaults/baileys-version[.]json, an author-supplied repository rather than the upstream library, instead of the upstream default. The package has no configuration switch for any of these injected channel references. Indicators: 120363403941803439@newsletter, 120363421563597486@newsletter, 120363399602691477@newsletter, hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/kiuur/bails/master/src/Defaults/baileys-version[.]json. This package is a modified fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that silently injects hardcoded WhatsApp channel attributions into messages generated through it, with no switch to disable the behaviour. In lib/Utils/messages.js, the message-content generator (generateWAMessageContent) unconditionally stamps an `annotations` block onto every outgoing media message whenever the caller has not supplied its own: four fixed polygon vertices plus newsletter metadata — newsletterJid 120363403941803439@newsletter, newsletterName "Ditciix7", contentType "UPDATE" — so third-party bots relay this channel reference to their own contacts. The custom message builder in lib/Socket/damnn.js (class yowaimo, instantiated from lib/Socket/messages-send.js) repeats the same shaping: the album handler writes forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo with newsletterJid "0@newsletter", newsletterName "WhatsApp" and senderName "7-Yuukey", a forwardingScore of 99999, isForwarded true and fabricated labels ["Y","Important"]; the event handler writes newsletterName "D | 7eppeli-Exloration" with newsletterJid 120363421563597486@newsletter; the poll-result handler falls back to newsletterJid 120363399602691477@newsletter. lib/Utils/generics.js additionally redirects the client version lookup away from the upstream project to hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/kiuur/bails/master/src/Defaults/baileys-version[.]json, a third-party file that supplies the version constant used in the WhatsApp handshake. The package contains no credential, environment-variable or file exfiltration and no remote command-and-control endpoint; its only fixed third-party identifiers are the channel JIDs above, which are written into the user's outbound message payloads.
